title: How can we get the most popular game from the list?
description: A list holds the favourite game of thirty one children, but the most popular game is hidden in it. The video groups the names by game, counts each group and compares the counts, and Keeko asks where else counting choices helps.
teaching_notes: One idea: bring equal answers together, count each group, then compare the counts. Watch for children who pick a winner by looking at the list without counting.

source: We can't yet see the most popular game. How can we get it from this list?
video_script.why: The child sees that grouping and counting turns a long list into an answer.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own list of the favourite games of 31 children
video_script.anchor: the favourite-games list that Ziva is showing
video_script.payoff_line: Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by eight children.

names.Ziva: girl who makes the favourite-games list with Naresh
names.Ruhee: teacher who buys sweets by the class preferences

maths_rules: Kabaddi 6, hockey 8, cricket 6, satoliya 5, football 4, badminton 2.
6 + 8 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 31, the number of children in the list.
8 is larger than 6, 6, 5, 4 and 2, so hockey is the most popular.
video_script.design: The book's list of thirty one children, regrouped into six boxes by game, then the six counts side by side.

beats.on_screen: title card with a long list of children and their favourite games in mixed order; a speech bubble from the children says we cannot see it yet

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the list
marks.list: the list fills line by line, one line for each child
marks.ask: a question mark lights up beside the list

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the list Ziva made.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The list shows the favourite game of thirty one children, in no special order.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The children cannot yet see the most popular game.
How can we get it from this list?

beats.on_screen: the list and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the list again with the same games coloured alike and scattered among the lines

marks.scatter: the lines of the same game light up in the same colour, far from each other
marks.bring: arrows show equal colours needing to come together

narration: <bookmark mark='scatter'/>The same game shows up on many lines, far from each other.
<bookmark mark='bring'/>To compare the games, we must bring the same games together.
Then each game becomes a group that we can count.

beats.on_screen: Given: the list of 31 children and their favourite games

marks.given: the list is written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a list of thirty one children and the favourite game of each.

beats.on_screen: To find: the most popular game

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the most popular game in the list.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: group the names by game; six boxes labelled Kabaddi, Hockey, Cricket, Satoliya, Football and Badminton, with the names moving into their boxes

marks.group: the names move into the six boxes, one box for each game

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step one, group the names by game, because equal answers must sit together.
There are six games, so we make six groups.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: count each group; Kabaddi 6, Hockey 8, Cricket 6, Satoliya 5, Football 4, Badminton 2

marks.count: the six boxes are counted one after another and a count appears under each

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the names in each group.
Kabaddi has six, hockey eight, and cricket six.
Satoliya has five, football four, and badminton two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the six counts; the largest count is circled

marks.compare: the six counts are set side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='compare'/>Step three, compare the six counts with each other.
<bookmark mark='largest'/>Eight is larger than all the other counts.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by 8 children
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by eight children.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a teacher at the board with five sweets drawn beside the names jalebi, gulab jamun, gujiya, barfi and rasgulla, and a hand raised by each child

marks.teacher: the teacher and the five sweets appear
marks.count: a count appears beside each sweet as the hands are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='teacher'/>Keeko asks where else counting choices helps.
Ruhee is a teacher who wanted to bring sweets for the class.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The teacher asked each child for a choice and counted them for each sweet.
Those counts told the teacher how many sweets of each kind to buy.
